subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 9-month-old girl is brought for evaluation of an enlarging abdomen and loss of previously acquired motor skills. She was born to nonconsanguineous Ashkenazi Jewish parents. Examination shows an alert but hypotonic infant with the liver and spleen palpable 5 cm below the costal margins and a cherry-red spot in each macula. Bone marrow aspiration shows numerous lipid-laden foam cells.
question: Deficiency of which of the following enzymes is most likely responsible?
explanation_correct: Sphingomyelinase deficiency causes Niemann-Pick disease, in which sphingomyelin and cholesterol accumulate in both reticuloendothelial cells and neurons. Storage in macrophages produces foam cells and massive hepatosplenomegaly, and neuronal storage explains the cherry-red spot and progressive neurodegeneration. The combination of a cherry-red spot with hepatosplenomegaly distinguishes Niemann-Pick disease from Tay-Sachs disease.

explanation_incorrect.A: Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes Tay-Sachs disease, which also produces a cherry-red spot but characteristically lacks hepatosplenomegaly and foam cells.
explanation_incorrect.B: Glucocerebrosidase deficiency causes Gaucher disease, in which the marrow cells are crumpled tissue paper macrophages and no cherry-red spot occurs.
explanation_incorrect.C: Arylsulfatase A deficiency causes metachromatic leukodystrophy, a demyelinating disorder without hepatosplenomegaly.
explanation_incorrect.D: Galactocerebrosidase deficiency causes Krabbe disease, characterized by globoid cells and destruction of oligodendrocytes.

educationalObjective: A cherry-red macular spot together with hepatosplenomegaly and foam cells in an infant points to Niemann-Pick disease, caused by sphingomyelinase deficiency.
